tour.name: Kanchanaburi Private Day Trip: Bridge on the River Kwai, the Death Railway & Erawan Falls
tour.subtitle: A private day of history and nature with a licensed guide and car: the war cemetery and museum of the Thailand–Burma Railway, the Bridge on the River Kwai, a ride on the Death Railway along the Wang Pho viaduct, and a swim in the turquoise pools of Erawan Falls.

tour.overview:
In 1942 and 1943, the Japanese army built a railway 415 kilometres long through the jungles and mountains between Thailand and Burma to supply its troops. More than 60,000 Allied prisoners of war and some 200,000 Asian labourers were forced to build it; about 12,000 prisoners and up to 90,000 labourers died from disease, starvation and brutality, giving it the name the Death Railway. The bridge over the Khwae Yai river, made famous by the 1957 film, still carries trains today. Upstream, the forests of the Tenasserim hills hide some of Thailand's most beautiful waterfalls.

This private day combines the history of the railway with the nature of Kanchanaburi province, with a licensed guide and a car. You visit the war cemetery and museum, walk on the bridge, ride a section of the railway along a wooden viaduct clinging to a cliff above the river, and end with a swim at Erawan Falls.

AT A GLANCE
• Duration: about 12 hours
• Start and end: your hotel in Bangkok
• Type: private tour with licensed guide, car and driver, train ride
• Booking: on request – we confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay only then
• Level: moderate; the walk up Erawan Falls is about 2 km on forest trails

WHAT YOU SEE
• The Kanchanaburi War Cemetery.
• The Thailand–Burma Railway Centre.
• The Bridge on the River Kwai.
• The Death Railway and the Wang Pho viaduct.
• Erawan National Park and its falls.

WHY THIS WORKS
The railway, the bridge and the falls are far apart; the car links them and meets you at the station, so you can ride the most dramatic part of the line.

WHO IT SUITS
History lovers, veterans' families and nature lovers who want a full day out of Bangkok.

WHO MAY PREFER ANOTHER TOUR
If you prefer a shorter day, choose Ayutthaya or the floating markets.

PRACTICAL INFORMATION
The train ride is in an ordinary third-class carriage with open windows: simple but atmospheric. Erawan National Park charges a foreign visitor fee and closes the falls trail in the late afternoon.

days.name: The war cemetery and railway museum, the Bridge on the River Kwai, the Death Railway and Erawan Falls
days.description:
What to expect: the history of the Thailand–Burma Railway and a jungle waterfall, with a licensed guide, private car, train ride, tickets and lunch.

Your guide and driver collect you at your hotel at 6:30 for the drive west, about two and a half hours. In Kanchanaburi you visit the War Cemetery, where 6,982 Allied prisoners of war, most of them British, Australian and Dutch, lie in rows of bronze plaques among neat lawns and flowers. Opposite, the Thailand–Burma Railway Centre tells the story of the line, how it was surveyed and built by hand, and the lives of the prisoners and labourers, with objects, letters and photographs.

You walk onto the Bridge on the River Kwai. The curved steel spans were brought from Java by the Japanese and assembled by prisoners; two of them were destroyed by Allied bombing in 1945 and replaced after the war with the straight sections you see today. At the station you board the train for the most spectacular part of the line, the Wang Pho viaduct, where the track runs on a wooden trestle along a cliff above the river. Your driver meets you at Tham Krasae station, and you have lunch at a restaurant overlooking the water.

In the afternoon you drive into Erawan National Park, about an hour away. The falls, named after the three-headed elephant of Hindu myth that the top tier is said to resemble, drop through seven tiers of limestone pools coloured emerald and turquoise by the minerals in the water. You walk up through the forest as far as you like and swim in the pools among small fish that nibble your feet. You drive back to Bangkok, arriving at about 19:00.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
06:30 – Pick-up at your hotel in Bangkok.
09:00 – Kanchanaburi War Cemetery.
09:30 – Thailand–Burma Railway Centre.
10:30 – Bridge on the River Kwai.
11:00 – Train on the Death Railway to Tham Krasae.
12:30 – Lunch by the river.
14:00 – Erawan Falls and swim.
16:30 – Drive back to Bangkok.
19:00 – Back at your hotel.

GOOD TO KNOW
• Train times are fixed and occasionally change; we adapt the order of the day.
• Hellfire Pass, a cutting dug by prisoners, with its excellent museum, can replace Erawan Falls.
• A night in a raft house on the river can be added.

INCLUDED: private car and driver, licensed guide, museum ticket, train ride, Erawan National Park entrance, lunch, bottled water, hotel pick-up and drop-off.
NOT INCLUDED: drinks with lunch, tips.

Overnight: none.
Meals: lunch.

faq.question: How does booking on request work?
faq.answer: You choose a date and the number of travellers and send the request. Nothing is charged. We confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay online only when the tour is confirmed.

faq.question: Is it a long day?
faq.answer: About 12 hours, with roughly 5 hours of driving. If you can, spend a night in Kanchanaburi to enjoy it at a slower pace.

faq.question: Is the train ride included?
faq.answer: Yes, a ride on the most scenic section of the line, including the Wang Pho viaduct, in a simple open-window carriage.

faq.question: Can we swim at Erawan Falls?
faq.answer: Yes, in several of the pools. Bring a swimsuit and towel; there are changing rooms near the entrance.

faq.question: Are the entrance fees included?
faq.answer: Yes: the railway museum and Erawan National Park. The war cemetery is free.

faq.question: Is lunch included?
faq.answer: Yes, by the river. Vegetarian and other diets are easy to arrange.

faq.question: Is it suitable for children?
faq.answer: Yes. Children love the train and the waterfall; the history is told at a level that suits them. Child seats are provided free of charge on request.

faq.question: Is it suitable for people with limited mobility?
faq.answer: Partly. The cemetery, museum and bridge are easy; the train has high steps, and the waterfall trail is uneven.

faq.question: Can we visit Hellfire Pass?
faq.answer: Yes, instead of Erawan Falls. Its museum and memorial walk are among the most moving places of the railway's history.

faq.question: Should we tip?
faq.answer: Tips are appreciated in Thailand but never required.

faq.question: What should we wear?
faq.answer: Light clothes, a swimsuit, shoes with grip that can get wet, a hat and insect repellent.

faq.question: What is the best time of year?
faq.answer: November to February is cool and dry. The falls are fullest from August to November, after the rains.

faq.question: What is the cancellation policy?
faq.answer: You can cancel free of charge up to 24 hours before the tour. Until your request is confirmed, nothing is charged at all.
